So this weekend is guys weekend (around 20 guys over the course of the weekend, maybe 10 at a time.) Most of them accept that I'm vegan, although I still get the comments whenever we eat together. This will probably be amplified as there is going to be a pig roast, and of course everything is going to be made on the BBQ. (But, but... bacon?)

Pretty much I need help finding recipes that I can make that I can just throw on the grill with no hassle. I don't want to be that one fussy looking eater spending all this time dicing food when the boys are having a bbq. I've always found homemade burgers don't fair well on the bbq and usually need the oven or pan. I've found some great soy sausages, but only want them for maybe 2 of the 6 meals (breakfast is fine with oatmeal.) Might to tofu kebabs, but was thinking of avoiding tofu for various reasons.

Fortunately, there is a former vegetarian (still aware of issues), and should be an (almost) vegan guy there too.

tl:dr - need some recipes that look likes total bro food as I want to avoid stupid comments over a guys weekend.
Need help finding good "Bro" recipes for a guy weekend.
BBQ is tough. What about making a chili sin carne? Lots of beans, onions, peppers and, to get the right texture, pearl barley and steel cut oats. Most people won't notice that it has no meat.

Why not seitan? I haven't tried it on a classic bbq yet, but I guess it should do the job. I don't have any specific recipe, but this would be the direction I would think of. I would suggest you to look for some seitan recipe with more fat, as it will be necessary for the grilling.

Good luck! :)
I'd second seitan. You can make some awesome riblets that grill well and the BBQ sauce helps with sticking.
i suggest falafels ok not bbq thing but everyone will love them in a wrap with salad even better!

This might not sound like "bro" food, but often when I have a get-together with my omni friends/family I take this: Chickpea Salad

It says sandwiches, but I always make it like a dip and take crackers or chips with it. Everybody loves it. Everybody! Oh, and I always add mustard to give it a tangier taste.

And guys love to dip into things. So there you go! ;)
this one looks good if you like tempeh: Tempeh BBQ

https://www.morningstarfarms.com/products/details/morningstar-farms-hickory-bbq-riblets-product.html

Those things are so much like a mcrib it isn't funny, slap a couple buns on the grill and load the riblet meat on them and it'll look like you're eating pork BBQ.

If you're looking for a little more work http://www.baked-in.com/2014/06/30/vegan-barbecue-ribs/

And don't forget Mexican corn on the cob - simple is just hitting it heavy with paprika cumin and chili powder, otherwise go nuts http://www.onegreenplanet.org/vegan-recipe/easy-elote-with-a-twist/

If you wast a damn delicious Burger, I would recommend some FieldRoast Patties. If you want to go all out... Make a chia egg(chia and water) to roll the burger in, next roll them in coconut, throw it on the grill. The burger damn good to begin with, but the coconut adds a nice flavor/texture. You can also add a slice of their FieldRoast brand Celebration roast, and a few slices of tempeh bacon, add everything together and you get what my local health food bistro calls "The Herbivore". It's fairly impossible to describe how beautiful this thing tastes, so you'll have to take my word for it.

If you are looking for something un-fussy, in addition to the great things that have already been suggested, try the pre-made vegan burgers from Sweet Earth. I've also thrown the Tofurky sausages on the grill with great success. Both are easy peasy.

Giant portobello burgers. Seriously you can't go wrong. Get some Montreal steak seasoning, and follow the directions on the back to make marinade. Let them (do 4-5) soak floor about a half hour. Then their your burgers on the grill first cuz they don't take as long as meat. Have a whole one yourself, then cut the others in half in full burger forms with buns and the works.

Then while they are hungry smelling their meat cook, tell them they can try some of your extras cuz you "think you made way too many.". Then mention the Montreal steak seasoning, you can put it on french fries, or anything. When you marinade them, then grill then, mushrooms seriously are the best - I've done this before and now I have a few meat-eaters that get excited when I tell them I was thinking about then at the store and bought extras!

Also if you want some good vegan chip/pretzel/french fries/whatever dips, get a few containers of your favorite soy cream cheese and soy mayo and mix in either taco seasoning packets or regular seasoning salt. Let them hang out in the fridge for a few hours (or overnight?) And you will be the dip king!!!!
